skill.name: orca-cli
skill.description: Operate Orca-managed worktrees, terminals, automations, embedded browser tabs, and emulator surfaces through the public Orca CLI.
skill.summary: CLI guidance for controlling Orca-managed coding workspaces.
skill.author: stablyai

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration language was found in SKILL.md. Many static hits are Markdown formatting false positives, but several examples are real Orca CLI workflows that create worktrees, launch agents, send terminal input, schedule automations, and control browser or emulator state. These capabilities are legitimate for the skill and should require explicit user intent and narrow scoping.

remediation.issue: Powerful Orca CLI actions can change worktrees, terminals, agents, automations, browser tabs, and emulator state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent guidance before destructive actions, terminal sends, agent launches, automation runs, browser eval, cookie reads, uploads, and emulator exec commands.

remediation.issue: Embedded browser commands can access sensitive page data and run page-side actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require user-provided targets for navigation and avoid cookie, network, screenshot, upload, eval, or exec operations unless the user directly requests them.

remediation.issue: Scheduled automations and setup hooks can run code later or under repository policy.
remediation.suggestion: Default new automations to disabled during setup, disclose the schedule and provider, and require confirmation before setup run or run-hooks modes.

content.value_statement: Orca projects often span worktrees, terminals, automations, and embedded browser tabs. This skill gives agents a precise CLI workflow for managing those Orca surfaces.
actual_capabilities: Check Orca status and list repos, worktrees, terminals, and active contexts using JSON CLI output.
Create Orca worktrees, manage parent lineage, set comments, and update workspace status.
Start Codex or Claude agents in Orca terminals and send handoff prompts.
Read, wait on, create, split, rename, stop, switch, and close Orca terminal sessions.
Create, edit, run, inspect, and remove scheduled Orca automations for repos or workspaces.
Control Orca embedded browser tabs and Orca emulator surfaces through typed CLI commands.
limitations: Requires the Orca CLI to be installed and Orca to be running for most workflows.
Controls only Orca-managed worktrees, embedded browser tabs, terminals, and emulator surfaces.
Commands can modify local repositories, terminals, browser state, and scheduled automations.
Advanced orchestration and emulator workflows may require the dedicated companion skills.

use_cases.title: Hand Off Coding Work
use_cases.description: Create a clean Orca worktree, start an agent, and pass a focused task brief with the right lineage.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers using Orca with AI agents

use_cases.title: Inspect Active Agent Sessions
use_cases.description: List terminals, read recent output, wait for idle state, and send the next prompt only when appropriate.

use_cases.title: Automate Orca Workspace Tasks
use_cases.description: Create scheduled prompts for repo reviews, issue triage, or workspace summaries with clear provider choices.
use_cases.target_user: Developer teams maintaining recurring AI workflows

prompt_templates.title: Check Orca State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca CLI to check whether Orca is running, then list my active worktrees and terminals. Summarize what is available.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Handoff Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an independent Orca worktree for this task and start Codex there. Send a concise task brief and report the new worktree details.

prompt_templates.title: Review Terminal Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the active Orca terminal, read its latest output, wait for idle state if needed, and tell me whether it needs a follow-up prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Browser and Automation Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Orca CLI to inspect embedded browser tabs and scheduled automations for this workspace. Recommend the narrowest safe next command for each surface.

output_examples.output: Orca is running. The active worktree has two terminals, one idle agent session, and no browser tab requiring attention.

output_examples.input: Hand this bug investigation to another agent.
output_examples.output: Created an independent Orca worktree for the investigation and started a Codex terminal with the task brief. I stopped monitoring after the handoff.

output_examples.input: Review the embedded browser state before continuing.
output_examples.output: The active browser tab is loaded and has current element references. A fresh snapshot is available before any click or form action.

best_practices: Run a status check before choosing worktree, terminal, automation, browser, or emulator commands.
Use JSON output and the narrowest Orca selector that matches the requested scope.
Read terminal or browser state before sending input unless the next action is explicit.
anti_patterns: Using raw git worktree, Playwright, simctl, or ad hoc terminal control when Orca state is required.
Sending terminal input, browser eval, cookie reads, uploads, or emulator exec commands without explicit user intent.
Monitoring a full handoff after ownership has moved to another agent or worktree.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls Orca-managed worktrees, terminals, repos, automations, embedded browser tabs, and emulator surfaces through Orca CLI commands.

faq.question: Does it require Orca?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require the Orca CLI and a running Orca app or Orca-managed workspace.

faq.question: Can it start other AI agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents how to create Orca terminals or worktrees that launch Codex, Claude, or Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: Can it control normal browser windows?
faq.answer: No. Browser commands are for Orca embedded tabs. External browsers or desktop UI need other tools.

faq.question: Is it safe for automated use?
faq.answer: Use caution. It can run commands, send terminal input, schedule prompts, and control browser or emulator state.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use orchestration or emulator companion skills when you need advanced task coordination or detailed mobile simulator control.
